name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a D+15 partisan lean
Incumbent Rob Menendez has a large financial advantage, with nearly $2 million raised and outside support
No general-election polls or expert ratings; the strongest opposition is an independent with no visible fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democratic side around 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Menendez: a D+15 district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising position against an independent challenger with no reported money. Markets agree, pricing the Democratic side near 95%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 23 points.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the independent challenger gaining traction, or a major scandal involving the incumbent, would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez, the Democratic incumbent in New Jersey's 8th District, seeks re-election in a seat with a D+15 partisan lean. He has raised nearly $2 million and holds about $680,000 on hand, with outside groups adding more than $900,000 in support and nothing in opposition. His principal challenger, independent Aristotle Eliopoulos, has no reported fundraising, and no other candidate on the ballot shows meaningful resources.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Democratic side at about 95%. The combination points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the incumbent favored by a margin in the low twenties.
